items.statement:
Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$ and a real stability parameter $\zeta>0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with Hermitian structures. The positive-FI stable complex ADHM quotient $X_{k,N}^\zeta$ is the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of quadruples $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$, satisfying $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and the condition that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$ for all words of length $m\geq0$ and $w\in W$. This is the positive stability chamber; it is not, by definition, the zero-FI regular quotient or the moduli space of anti-self-dual connections.

Let $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^\times)^2\times(\mathbb C^\times)^N$ act algebraically, and let $K=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ be its maximal compact subgroup. The action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Thus $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. Write $\epsilon_i=c_1^K(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^K(e_\alpha)$; each has mass dimension one in units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $q$ be a dimensionless formal charge-counting variable.

Assume the complexification of this action gives each $X_{k,N}^\zeta$ a smooth separated finite-type complex structure of dimension $2kN$, a finite invariant affine atlas, and a finite proper fixed locus $F_{k,N}$. Extend the complex torus to $T_m=T_{\mathbb C}\times\mathbb C_m^\times$ with maximal compact subgroup $K_m=K\times S_m^1$; the flavor factor acts trivially on $X_{k,N}^\zeta$. Let $\widetilde m$ be the degree-two equivariant first Chern class of its defining flavor character, let $L_{-1}$ be the associated line of inverse flavor character, and set
$$\mathcal E_{\widetilde m}=c_{2kN}^{T_m}(TX_{k,N}^\zeta\otimes L_{-1})\in H_{T_m}^{4kN}(X_{k,N}^\zeta;\mathbb Q).$$
At a fixed point with tangent weights $w_1,\ldots,w_{2kN}$, its restriction is $\prod_{j=1}^{2kN}(w_j-\widetilde m)$. Let $S_{T_m}$ be generated by the first Chern classes of nontrivial integral characters of $T_m$, put $R_{T_m}=H^*(BK_m;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N,\widetilde m]$, and let $K_{N,m}=\operatorname{Frac}(R_{T_m})$. When the character-localized Borel–Moore concentration map and proper fixed-locus trace define $p_{k,*}^{\mathrm{loc}}$, set
$$I_{k,N}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)=p_{k,*}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigl(\mathcal E_{\widetilde m}\cap[X_{k,N}^\zeta]_{K_m}\bigr)\in S_{T_m}^{-1}R_{T_m}\subset K_{N,m}.$$
This is a localized pushforward, not an ordinary pushforward along a nonproper map. The concentration isomorphism and trace are required inputs and are not asserted to exist by this definition.

When these data are supplied for every $k\geq0$, define the coefficientwise formal series
$$Z_{N,\mathrm{adj}}^{\mathrm{loc}}(q;\widetilde m)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k I_{k,N}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)\in K_{N,m}\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
It has no asserted analytic convergence. In the source's Euclidean convention the real mass $m_E$ has mass dimension one, $m=i m_E$, and the equivariant mass is $\widetilde m=m+(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)/2$. For the adopted round $S^4_r$ model, $N=2$, $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=r^{-1}$, and hence $\widetilde m=i m_E+r^{-1}$. This mass shift is a source-qualified convention. The S4 postulate assumes a supersymmetry-compatible noncommutative regulator agreeing near each pole with the flat-space regulator; it does not construct that regulator or a continuum path-integral measure.

items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional rank-one, charge-one stable ADHM quotient and its mass-twisted localized Borel–Moore coefficient. It makes no continuum gauge-theory claim.
items.axiom_base: ZF + the choice strength inherited from the normalized equivariant Borel–Moore suppliers; the finite scalar quotient calculation itself uses no choice.
items.design_state: Local complete scalar quotient and mass-inserted fixed-point proof added to support the rank-one B-page example.
items.statement:
Let $V=W=\mathbb C$, let $k=N=1$, and consider scalar ADHM data $(b_1,b_2,i,j)\in\mathbb C^4$ satisfying $ij=0$ and the stability condition $i\ne0$. Let $GL(V)=\mathbb C^\times$ act by $(b_1,b_2,i,j)\mapsto(b_1,b_2,\lambda i,\lambda^{-1}j)$, and let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^2\times\mathbb C^\times_h$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(b_1,b_2,i,j)=(t_1b_1,t_2b_2,h^{-1}i,t_1t_2h j)$. Write $X$ for the geometric quotient of the stable locus. Extend $T$ by a flavor torus $\mathbb C_m^\times$ acting trivially on $X$, with additive character $\widetilde m$. The quotient is isomorphic to $\mathbb C^2$ with coordinates $b_1,b_2$, the fixed locus is the origin, and the tangent weights there are $\epsilon_1=c_1(t_1)$ and $\epsilon_2=c_1(t_2)$. If the localized Borel–Moore pushforward of the complex-oriented fundamental class with insertion $c_2^{T_m}(TX\otimes L_{-1})$ is defined, where $L_{-1}$ is the inverse flavor line of weight $-\widetilde m$, then the charge-one coefficient is
$$I_{1,1}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)=\frac{(\epsilon_1-\widetilde m)(\epsilon_2-\widetilde m)}{\epsilon_1\epsilon_2}.$$
At charge zero the quotient is a point with rank-zero insertion and coefficient $1$.

items.statement:
Fix $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and $\zeta>0$. Let $X_{k,N}^\zeta$ be the positive-FI stable complex ADHM quotient with rotation and dual-framing torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acting by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$. Write $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$, and assume these weights are algebraically independent. Let $q$ be dimensionless and formal. For an $N$-tuple of partitions $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$, each $Y_\alpha$ a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$, put $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j$, and $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Assume the complexified torus acts algebraically on a smooth separated finite-type variety of complex dimension $2kN$, with a finite invariant affine atlas and finite proper fixed locus. Assume the fixed points and tangent characters are exactly those of the positive-FI ADHM theorem. Extend $T$ by a flavor circle acting trivially on the quotient, with additive character $\widetilde m$, and let $\mathcal E_{\widetilde m}=c_{2kN}^{T_m}(TX_{k,N}^\zeta\otimes L_{-1})$ be the top Chern insertion for the inverse flavor line. Assume its localized Borel–Moore pushforward is defined by the proper-fixed-locus construction and satisfies the noncompact localization formula. For the source-reported N=2* convention, set $m=i m_E$ for real Euclidean mass $m_E$ and $\widetilde m=m+(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)/2$.

At a fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}X_{k,N}^\zeta)=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
For each tangent character $\chi$, write $w_\chi=c_1^T(\chi)$ and let $E_{\vec Y}=\prod_\chi w_\chi$ and $N_{\vec Y}(\widetilde m)=\prod_\chi(w_\chi-\widetilde m)$, with multiplicities. Then the mass-inserted coefficient and formal series are
$$I_{k,N}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)=\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}\frac{N_{\vec Y}(\widetilde m)}{E_{\vec Y}},\qquad Z_{N,\mathrm{adj}}^{\mathrm{loc}}(q;\widetilde m)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}\frac{N_{\vec Y}(\widetilde m)}{E_{\vec Y}}\in\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N,\widetilde m)\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$

For the adopted round $S^4_r$ N=2* model, specialize to $N=2$, $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=r^{-1}$ and $\widetilde m=i m_E+r^{-1}$, with $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$ on the model's continued Coulomb contour. The source assumes, but does not construct, the supersymmetry-compatible noncommutative S4 regulator agreeing near each pole with the flat-space regulator. The displayed identity is a formal fixed-point calculation for the regulated local factor; it does not prove existence of that regulator, a continuum functional measure, the full S4 partition function, or convergence of the series.
